deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Riemann is treating a displacement field (x',y',z') of a medium (the aether, given the bundle title) as functions of (x,y,z,t). The forces (X,Y,Z) are tied to the incompressibility condition div(x',y',z') = 0 through a Lagrange multiplier λ. The previous page derives X = ∂λ/∂x, Y = ∂λ/∂y, Z = ∂λ/∂z, i.e. dλ = X dx + Y dy + Z dz. That is: the virtual work ∫(X δx' + Y δy' + Z δz') dV is, up to boundary terms, −∫ λ δ(div x') dV, which vanishes for admissible (divergence-free) variations.

This page writes the virtual work over space-time and shows it is (minus) the variation of a quadratic action.

Line 1: ∫ (X δx' + Y δy' + Z δz') dx dy dz dt.

Line 2: Here X, Y, Z are identified with the kinetic residuals (this identification is implicit; the reading is mine):
 X = c²(∂²x'/∂x² + ∂²x'/∂y² + ∂²x'/∂z²) − ∂²x'/∂t², i.e. X = c²Δx' − x'_tt,
 and likewise for Y with y' and Z with z' (the '+ . . .' rows). So the integral equals ∫ Σ_i {c² Δx'_i − ∂²x'_i/∂t²} δx'_i dx dy dz dt.

Line 3: Integrate by parts once in each of x, y, z, t. With '. .' standing for boundary terms, this gives
 − ∫ { c² (∂x'/∂x ∂δx'/∂x + ∂x'/∂y ∂δx'/∂y + ∂x'/∂z ∂δx'/∂z) − ∂x'/∂t ∂δx'/∂t } dx dy dz dt,
 with analogous terms for y' and z'.

Line 4: Since u_a δu_a = δ(½ u_a²) (my step), this equals
 boundary terms − δ ∫ ½ { c² ((∂x'/∂x)² + (∂x'/∂y)² + (∂x'/∂z)²) − (∂x'/∂t)² } dx dy dz dt,
 plus the y' and z' analogues.

Combined with the previous page, this says the motion is a stationary point of the action
 S = ∫ ½ Σ_i [ (∂x'_i/∂t)² − c² |∇x'_i|² ] dx dy dz dt
under the constraint div x' = 0, with λ as multiplier. The resulting equations are
 ∂²x'/∂t² = c² Δx' − ∇λ, div x' = 0.
These are the equations of an incompressible elastic medium carrying only transverse waves of speed c. This is the classical model of a luminiferous aether, closely related to Riemann's 'Gravitation und Licht' fragments.

The page thus establishes the Hamilton/Lagrange variational form of the vector wave equation with incompressibility constraint.
errors: No mathematical errors. The sign after the double integration by parts is correct: ∫(c²Δu − u_tt)δu = bdry − ∫(c²∇u·∇δu − u_t δu_t).
The final line requires the factor 1/2 inside δ∫ for exact equality. The written symbol is unclear but is most plausibly ½.
The identification of X with c²Δx' − x'_tt is not stated on the page. It is implicit, possibly via a sign or definitional convention set up elsewhere in the bundle.

results.what: Virtual work of the inertial plus elastic forces of the wave equation equals minus the variation of a space-time action with density ½(c²|∇u|² − u_t²)
results.modern_name: Hamilton's principle / Lagrangian density ½(u_t² − c²|∇u|²) for the wave equation
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Mécanique analytique, 1788); Hamilton (1834-35); for elastic aether Green (1839) and MacCullagh (1839)

results.what: Incompressibility constraint handled by a Lagrange multiplier λ acting as a pressure: u_tt = c²Δu − ∇λ, div u = 0
results.modern_name: Lagrange multiplier / pressure for an incompressible elastic medium (transverse-wave aether)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (multipliers); Cauchy and Green (incompressible elastic aether, 1830s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard variational derivation of the wave equation for an incompressible elastic aether, well known by the 1830s-40s (Green, MacCullagh). It fits Riemann's known aether and gravitation-light Nachlass fragments and contains nothing new.
